assumptions: The service begins as clerical document QA and coordination rather than regulated energy certification or legal representation.
Permissioned pilot files and GDPR-compliant processor agreements can be obtained without relying on unconsented beneficiary data.
Officially reported program activity remains directionally representative of near-term closeout opportunities, but not of the addressable paid segment.
Published competitor prices indicate market context but do not prove realized purchases, conversion or customer satisfaction.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid pilots with unrelated installers showing realized price, defect prevention, turnaround and repeat purchases; fully loaded case economics including rework, specialist escalation, insurance and acquisition cost; signed service, referral and data-processing agreements; a legal and insurance review defining the permissible scope; and measured evidence that integrations or a permissioned defect corpus produce a durable accuracy or speed advantage over bundled substitutes.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The pre-submission evidence gate is a real workflow position tied to subsidy payment, and official reporting confirms document errors and processing friction. The insight is useful but not novel: consultants, installers, energy specialists and public operators already address the same workflow.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Delayed reimbursement or installer collection can be materially painful, and published commercial offers support some willingness to pay for settlement help. However, those offers are not purchase evidence, no buyer interviews or paid pilots establish urgency, and free or PLN 200 substitutes challenge the proposed PLN 500-1,200 price.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Per-case fees can convert quickly and repeat with installer project volume, while a manual-to-automation path is capital-light. The proposed labor time, 55-70% contribution margin, CAC, overhead, realized price, repeat rate and 6,000-case wealth path are unmeasured; specialist review, rework, security and liability could keep this a labor-intensive service and compress owner earnings.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Polish retrofit installers with recurring Czyste Powietrze closeouts form a coherent, accessible beachhead, and official program activity indicates meaningful current volume. Addressable paid volume is nevertheless unknown and reduced by self-service, bundled assistance and publicly supported operators, while dependence on one subsidy program creates concentration risk.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: A standardized specialist desk could earn a useful position among smaller installers, especially through workflow integration and dependable turnaround. Presently the service lacks exclusive access, contracts, credentials, proprietary technology or a demonstrated performance edge, while adjacent incumbents can bundle closeout at low incremental cost.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Winning installer trust could support adjacent grant programs, broader compliance administration, audit coordination and workflow software. Those adjacencies are plausible but not evidenced, may require new rule expertise or credentials, and do not automatically inherit demand or distribution from this single-program wedge.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: A permissioned defect taxonomy, integrations and reviewer playbooks could improve over time, but none yet exists or has demonstrated a learning curve. Checklists and review operations appear replicable, access is informal and nonexclusive, data reuse may be constrained, and changing rules can erode accumulated process knowledge.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Focused turnaround, standardized QA and installer-oriented intake could be more convenient than fragmented handling. No measured reduction in defects, processing time or cost establishes a behavior-changing advantage, and existing competitors offer the same workflow either more cheaply or bundled free.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The program remains active at material scale and AI/OCR can lower the cost of document intake and checking. At the same time, 2026 rule changes demonstrate volatility, public operator support expands substitution, and the same automation is available to incumbents.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: The family installer relationship provides a credible, low-cost route to observe and test the workflow, and installer or auditor referrals fit the market. It is at-will, nonexclusive and excludes unconsented files; no signed channel, conversion evidence or observed CAC supports repeatable acquisition beyond the initial relationship.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder's analytics and AI skills, family operating context, modest capital need and part-time manual pilot make initial execution realistic. Scaling requires accurate reviewers, secure GDPR-compliant processing, clear authorization and credential boundaries, insurance, current rule maintenance and tight quality control because errors can delay customer payments.

highest_value_structural_change: Broaden from standalone closeout preparation into an embedded, contracted installer receivables-assurance workflow that captures documents throughout each project, integrates with installer operations and charges for demonstrably faster, lower-rework payment outcomes across multiple subsidy programs.
main_structural_strength: A concrete, recurring payment-adjacent workflow can be tested cheaply through the founder's family installer access and is well suited to systematic QA and AI-assisted automation.
primary_score_limiter: The standalone service has no demonstrated differentiation or defensible control point against low-priced, free-bundled and public substitutes, while its pricing and fully loaded economics remain unvalidated.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Direct substitutes already perform or bundle the same work: one provider advertises payment-application preparation for PLN 200, installers and energy specialists offer administration or settlement free with broader purchases, and public operators support eligible beneficiaries through final settlement.
